claims.text: SORTED, not raw set order. ``resolve_internal`` takes the FIRST match in these lists, so their order decides which file an ambiguous import binds to -- and iterating the set directly made that depend on PYTHONHASHSEED.
claims.why: The code iterates over sorted(known_files) and appends to by_basename and by_dir_tail in that sorted order. Thus the lists are in sorted order, not set order, stabilizing the first-match behavior for resolve_internal.

claims.text: On repos with repeated basenames (Marlin ships HAL/AVR/fastio.h, HAL/DUE/fastio.h, ...) the same source resolved to a different header on every process, silently changing dependencies/import_edges/fan_in.
claims.why: This claim refers to behavior before the fix (iterating set directly). The current code uses sorted order, so the claim is about a past state. The code in this chunk does not demonstrate the prior behavior; it only states it as motivation. The claim cannot be verified against the current code because it describes a previous version.

claims.text: Unified rel->rel internal import map (ALL languages) — powers the Move-4 symbol resolver; distinct from ``dep_edges`` whose Python keys are dotted.
claims.why: import_targets_by_rel is defined as defaultdict(set) and is populated for both Python (line 648) and other languages (line 658). It stores rel->rel mappings, while dep_edges for Python uses dotted module names (line 647). The comment accurately describes the distinction.

claims.text: Raw per-file type facts, keyed by rel. Collected for EVERY Python file, including shell files, and OUTSIDE the metric-withholding guard below -- exactly like import resolution and for the same reason: a real file whose annotation names a type declared in a vendored module must be resolvable, or the layer would report a gap that is an artifact of scoping rather than a fact about the code. The WITHHOLDING happens one layer down: ``resolve_type_graph(ignored=...)`` drops a withheld file's own facts, so a shell file contributes no node, no edge and no coverage number of its own. This dict never reaches ``modules``, ``all_units`` or ``build_resolver``.
claims.why: type_facts_by_rel is populated for every Python file regardless of ignored status (line 636: if spec.name == 'python': type_facts_by_rel[rel] = a.type_facts). It is not used in modules, all_units, or build_resolver within this chunk. The claim about resolve_type_graph is uncheckable because that function is not in this chunk, but the statement about this dict not reaching those structures is consistent with the code: type_facts_by_rel is only assigned, never referenced in this chunk.

claims.text: Inside the SAME withholding guard as total_chars on purpose: this is the denominator of the distill ratio, and its numerator only ever contains in-center files. A token total accumulated outside the guard would count ignored files as part of 'the repo the slice replaced', inflating the reduction headline.
claims.why: total_tokens is incremented inside the 'if rel not in ignored' block, same as total_chars. The comment explains the rationale, and the code matches the description.

claims.text: Per-file token cost is required by budgeted context planners. ``total_tokens`` alone cannot tell DSS whether a candidate fits, and falling back to LOC*8 makes the receipt deterministic but not tokenizer-true.  Additive: existing metric keys keep their meaning.
claims.why: The code stores a.n_tokens in modules[rel] as part of the metrics dict. This provides per-file token count. The comment explains the need, and the code implements it.

claims.text: Python resolution: precise, relative-aware, and resolved against the tables THIS file's own package root implies -- a center file against its center-relative view, a shell file against the unchanged repo-root view.
claims.why: The comment describes the behavior of py_naming.tables_for(rel) and resolve_python_imports. These functions are not defined in this chunk, so the claim about their behavior cannot be verified. The code calls them but does not reveal their implementation.

claims.text: Fold an alias spelling onto the file's ONE canonical name before it becomes an edge, so fan_in never counts a file twice.
claims.why: The code does: tgt = view.canon.get(raw_tgt, raw_tgt). This maps alias to canonical name if present, otherwise keeps original. This ensures consistent naming for edges.

claims.text: All other languages: best-effort, keyed by rel path (no dotted id).
claims.why: For non-Python languages, the code uses rel paths directly as keys in dep_edges (line 658: dep_edges[rel].add(tgt_rel)). No dotted module names are used.

claims.text: It runs AFTER the code pass because link resolution needs the whole file set -- same split as import resolution: extraction is per-file, resolution is whole-repo.
claims.why: The document pass code appears after the code pass loop. The comment states it runs after, and the code position confirms it.

claims.text: Link targets may be code OR another document; the resolvable universe is both. Deliberately NOT folded into ``by_basename``/``by_dir_tail``: those drive best-effort C/JS import resolution, where admitting a .md would let ``require('./README')`` bind to a document.
claims.why: known_all is constructed separately as known_files | doc_records rels. It is not added to by_basename or by_dir_tail. The comment explains the design choice, and the code matches: by_basename and by_dir_tail are not updated with doc records.

observations.what: by_dir_tail is populated only for files with a parent directory that has a tail (i.e., non-empty parent and tail). Files in root directory are not added.
total_chars and total_tokens are only updated for non-ignored files, but type_facts_by_rel is updated for all Python files regardless of ignored status.
For non-Python languages, dep_edges keys are relative paths (rel), while for Python they are dotted module names (src_mod). This is intentional but could cause confusion if mixed.
doc_units, doc_links, doc_totals are defined but not used in this chunk; they will be used in subsequent code.
